title: Choosing a security framework for incident & disclosure
transcript:
Security Lead: Alright team, let's discuss the data access control solution. We've been exploring options, and it seems Apache Ranger has gathered some traction.

On-Call Engineer: That's a bit concerning, I've heard it's got a steep learning curve.

Comms Lead: true, but remember, we've considered several options. Apache Sentry was rejected due to lack of support for cloud data stores, and Apache Knox due to reported performance issues with high concurrent requests.

Legal Counsel: Correct, and we also looked at an open-source RBAC system. However, it's not widely used in logistics operators, and long-term maintainability concerns were raised.

On-Call Engineer: Right, but Ranger is popular within our industry, and it has an extensive feature set addressing both team familiarity and long-term maintainability.

Security Lead: Exactly, and we have performance data from similar-sized companies running Ranger that we can look at.

Comms Lead: That being said, we do have a couple of caveats. We need to confirm its compatibility with our current data lake's Apache Hadoop version, and we'll need to ongoing evaluate its impact on system performance during peak hours.

Legal Counsel: Agreed. But I've also signed off on the provisional adoption of Apache Ranger for data access control.

On-Call Engineer: (sighs) Alright, I'll add it to my learning list.

Comms Lead: (off-topic) Hey, did anyone catch the game last night?

Security Lead: (off-topic) I did, it was a nail-biter! But let's get back to our topic, shall we?

Comms Lead: Definitely, back to work!

(end transcript)
document: Meeting Summary: Adoption of Apache Ranger for data access control was discussed. The on-call engineer voiced concerns regarding the learning curve for Ranger in the context of the logistics industry. The security lead and legal counsel were present. It was noted that Apache Sentry, an alternative, lacks support for cloud data stores. The popularity of Apache Ranger within the logistics industry was also mentioned. Further evaluation of Ranger's compatibility with our current data lake's Apache Hadoop version and its impact on system performance during peak hours is ongoing.
